newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia officials misuse $22 million in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia officials misuse $22 million in 1996.

text.p: Mongolia has brought charges against hundreds of officials accused of misusing 16 billion tugriks ($22 million) in government funds in 1996, officials said on Thursday.
The State Audit Board (SAB) had uncovered the losses from state coffers during investigations into the budget, state property and use of foreign aid, SAB chairman L. Javzmaa said.
"We revealed 16 billion tugriks in violations and losses, which is not a small amount of money," Javzmaa told a news conference.
The SAB had brought court charges against 213 officials, fined nearly 100 people some 1.3 million tugriks and taken disciplinary action against another 100 people, Javzmaa said.
"The State Audit Board was extremely busy," he said.

Among those accused of misusing funds were a former director of the commission regulating Mongolia's stock exchange and the former head of the Mongolian news agency Montsame, he said but gave no further details.
Officials had embezzled some 900 million tugriks in pension funds originally earmarked for herders and farmers, he said.
One official had lent out at least 111 million tugriks of pension funds, he said.
About 60 million tugriks from unemployment coffers had been used for building an apartment complex, he said.
The government had so far recovered some six billion tugriks and was chasing the other 10 billion, he said.
Mongolia's reformist government has launched large-scale inspections and overhauls of ministries and financial organs since it swept to power in elections last June.
